form_analysis.feedback: Exceptional aftercare form for lip blush tattoo removal addressing this highly vascular, mobile area. Comprehensive guidance on perioral swelling, herpes prophylaxis, and color-specific challenges. Strong emphasis on the extended healing timeline and realistic expectations.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser removal of LIP BLUSH/CONTOUR tattoos (permanent lip makeup). Lips are highly vascular, constantly mobile, and prone to herpes outbreaks. Lip pigments often contain red/orange tones that present specific removal challenges.

instructions.general_directive: Follow with extreme care. Lips swell significantly and require specific precautions. Herpes prophylaxis is NON-NEGOTIABLE.

sections.title: Lip Blush Specifics
sections.content: Lip tattoos use red/orange/pink iron oxide pigments placed in vermilion border. High vascularity increases bleeding/swelling. Constant movement affects healing. High risk of herpes simplex activation.

sections.title: Immediate Perioral Response
items: Significant lip swelling (2-3x normal size) for 3-5 days.
Difficulty eating, drinking, speaking for 2-3 days.
Cold compresses essential for swelling control.

sections.title: Herpes Prophylaxis (CRITICAL)
sections.content: Laser on lips ALWAYS triggers herpes in susceptible individuals. MUST take antiviral (Valtrex/Famvir) starting 2 days before and continuing 7 days after. If you feel tingling/itching, contact practitioner immediately for increased dosage.

sections.title: Vascular Considerations
items: More bleeding than other areas - apply pressure with clean gauze.
Ice cubes (wrapped) to constrict blood vessels.
Avoid blood thinners (aspirin, NSAIDs, alcohol) for 48 hours before/after.

sections.title: Color Challenges on Lips
items: Red/orange pigments: High risk of paradoxical darkening.
Test patch recommended due to high complication risk.

sections.title: Realistic Lip Removal Expectations
items: Complete removal often not possible without hypopigmentation.
Goal is often correction (lightening for new pigment) not complete removal.
Natural lip color may not fully return.
Risk of textural changes, loss of vermilion border definition.
